topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Networks: Planar Graphs and Euler's Formula
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Computer Science

lecture_lines: A tangled graph can be untangled.

sections.title: Euler's Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula relates V, E, and F.
The formula is V minus E plus F.
For planar graphs, this equals two.
Simple shapes like triangles prove this.
Every connected graph obeys this rule.
animations: Display the formula V - E + F = 2 in center with color #FFFFFF.
Draw a triangle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/triangle.svg] (V=3, E=3, F=2) using color #33FF57 lines.
Animate labels V=3, E=3, F=2 appearing near the triangle.
Highlight the calculation 3 - 3 + 2 = 2 using color #FF5733.
The equation flashes green indicating the equality holds true.

The resulting dual graph (triangular lattice) shown in #33FF57.
